office_does: A State Senator writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering the tax structure, school funding, criminal-justice statutes and housing rules, and confirms gubernatorial appointments.
race_blurb: Democratic incumbent John Lovick, a former State Patrol trooper, county sheriff and county executive, faces Republican Sherri Larkin, a Snohomish School Board director in her first legislative race. Lovick voted for the 2025 and 2026 state tax increases; Larkin runs on reducing the tax burden and restraining state spending.

candidates.summary: Incumbent State Senator since 2021, former Snohomish County Sheriff and Executive and longtime State Patrol trooper, whose record centers law-enforcement training and accountability standards and road safety.
highlights: Prime sponsor of SB 5974 (2026), setting eligibility and certification standards for police chiefs, marshals and sheriffs [S5]
Cites three new regional peace-officer academies and supports light rail to Everett and beyond [S1]
Voted for the 2026 tax on income over $1 million and the 2025 capital gains, excise and B&O tax increases [S8][S9][S10][S11]
Voted for EHB 1217 (2025 rent-increase limits) and ESHB 1296 (2025 amendments to the I-2081 parents' rights list) [S12][S13]

taxes.basis: Voted for ESSB 6346 (9.9% tax on income over $1 million) and for the 2025 capital gains/estate (ESSB 5813), excise (ESSB 5814) and B&O (ESHB 2081) tax increases.

housing.basis: Voted for EHB 1217, the 2025 limits on residential rent and fee increases; no campaign statement on housing.

safety.basis: Record centers law-enforcement capacity (three new regional police academies) and standards for law-enforcement leaders (SB 5974), framed around feeling safe; no stated prevention or diversion agenda.

experience.basis: Senator since 2021 after nine House years, plus service as county sheriff and executive; opponent has never held legislative office.

social.basis: Lists a Planned Parenthood endorsement and is endorsed by Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates; no statement of his own on reproductive or LGBTQ+ policy.

parental-rights.basis: Voted for ESHB 1296, which amended the I-2081 list of parent and guardian rights; no campaign statement on the topic.

candidates.summary: Snohomish School Board director since 2023 and former teacher, a first-time legislative candidate running on stronger schools, safer communities and smarter spending.
highlights: Says a rapidly expanding state government has left families "overtaxed and overburdened" [S1]
Pledges to restore "fiscal integrity" and reduce the burden on families and businesses [S1]
Wants safe neighborhoods "where law enforcement is supported" [S1]
Endorsers quoted on her site describe her school-board work in parental-rights terms [S3]

taxes.basis: Pamphlet says families are 'overtaxed and overburdened' and pledges to 'reduce the heavy burden on families and businesses'.

spending.basis: Criticizes a 'rapidly expanding state government' with 'programs that too often deliver no measurable results' and runs on 'Smarter Spending' and restoring fiscal integrity.

safety.basis: Calls for 'safe neighborhoods where law enforcement is supported'; no specific enforcement or prevention proposals.

experience.basis: First legislative race, with three years of school-board service, against a long-serving incumbent.

parental-rights.basis: Only endorser quotes on her site (parents 'should have a voice'; school-board work 'back toward ... parental rights'); no statement of her own.
